The '''''Vakbeor''-class cargo frigate''', also known as the '''Resistance Cargo Frigate''', was a type of hybrid [[cargo frigate]] design manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards]]. They were used by the [[Resistance]] [[Resistance navy|navy]] during its [[First Order-Resistance War|conflict]] with the [[First Order]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:TheVigil-RiseoftheResistance.png|thumb|250px|left|Aft view of the engines on a ''Vakbeor''-class cargo frigate]]
The ''Vakbeor''-class was envisioned as a combination of basic anti-[[pirate]] defenses with an extensive cargo capacity. Its light armament was made up of four [[laser cannon]]s; it also boasted two [[tractor beam projector]]s.<ref name="TLJICS" />

==History==
After the bankruptcy of [[Gallofree Yards, Inc.]], the [[Galactic Empire]] engineered the company's takeover by [[Kuat Drive Yards]]. KDY coupled existing Gallofree designs with elements of its own Nebulon frigate line to create the ''Vakbeor''-class. The new design would fare poorly on the galactic [[starship]] market, with many of them being dumped on the secondary market. Despite its initial role as an anti-pirate freighter, it became popular with pirate bands.<ref name="TLJICS" />

One ship, the ''[[Vigil]]'', was used by pirates until it was captured by the [[Resistance]], a [[New Republic]]-sponsored paramilitary group, in a [[Battle of Chasidron Shoals|battle]] off the [[Chasidron Shoals]].<ref name="TLJICS" /> The ''Vigil'' participated in the [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuation of D'Qar]] and the [[Battle of Oetchi]] where it was subsequently destroyed by a barrage of fire from First Order starships.<ref name="TLJ" />

During the [[Battle of Batuu|mission to Batuu]], several ''Vakbeor''-class cargo frigates were part of a fleet that engaged First Order [[Star Destroyer]]s above [[Batuu]] in a large space battle. One cargo frigate broadsided a Star Destroyer where Resistance recruits were attempting to escape, but was soon destroyed by a barrage of laser fire from the Star Destroyer.<ref name="Rise of the Resistance">{{GEAttr|Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance|Rise of the Resistance}}</ref>

In [[35 ABY]],<ref name="TROS Date">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] to one [[Standard year|year]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']]. As ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of ''The Force Awakens'' to [[34 ABY]], the events of ''The Rise of Skywalker'' must occur in [[35 ABY]].</ref> ''Vakbeor''-class cargo frigates were part of a [[Citizens' Fleet|fleet]] assembled by [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] to assist the Resistance during the [[Battle of Exegol|battle]] against the [[Sith Eternal military|Sith Eternal forces]] over the [[planet]] [[Exegol]].<ref name="Episode IX" />

{{Ship-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Vakbeor''-class cargo frigate appears in the [[2017]] [[Star Wars saga|''Star Wars'' saga]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']]. According to [[Jason Fry]], the vessel's class was named after the micro-animal [[Wikipedia:Tardigrade|Tardigrade]], or vac-bear, which his son fell in love with as a child.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://eleven-thirtyeight.com/2018/01/the-last-jedi-incredible-cross-sections-an-interview-with-jason-fry|text=The Last Jedi Incredible Cross-Sections – An Interview with Jason Fry|author=Nicholas W. Adams|date=2018-01-15|language=English|quote="For the Vigil I leaned into its odd hybrid look, carrying that through into the story of its creation and giving us a fun anecdote about a pirate battle to boot. The class name is kind of a funny story – I called it a Tardigrade class, after a weird little animal my son fell in love with as a small child. DK kicked that name back because they didn't want to use a real-world animal as a ship class, which I agreed with. So I came up with a gussied-up version of "vacuum bear" – Vakbeor — as a replacement, thinking I'd sub in something else later. By the time I got around to it, I'd decided I kinda liked Vakbeor and let it stand."|archivedate=20180120074250}}</ref>
